summary: Additive feature: @cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline's WasmEncryptionClient gains encryptQuery and encryptQueryBulk, minting EQL v3 query terms on Deno/edge. Both reuse the native client's shared index resolver and pre-FFI validators (contrary to the PR description, which says a local port was written), so inference and validation cannot drift from the native path. Existing encrypt/decrypt behaviour is unchanged. Scalar query types are verified end to end: CI ran the shared v3 family matrix through the WASM entry against real ZeroKMS and real Postgres/Supabase (Drizzle v3 integration jobs, both passed), and the Deno smoke suite against the built dist passed. The main residual risks are contract-level on a newly published, effectively irreversible API surface: the declared return type (EncryptedQuery | null) does not admit the bare selector string the searchableJson selector path returns, JSON containment/selector terms are only shape-checked, never matched against a database, and the docblock advises that query terms are safe to log-scrub less aggressively. Impact if these bite is medium; no plaintext or key-handling path is changed.

behaviour_changes.description: New public methods WasmEncryptionClient.encryptQuery(plaintext, {table, column, queryType?}) and encryptQueryBulk(terms) plus exported types WasmEncryptQueryOptions and WasmQueryTerm on the published ./wasm-inline subpath export. Released as a minor bump via changeset.

Index type/queryOp resolution and value validation (NaN/Infinity/out-of-int64 bigint, numeric-on-match) are delegated to the same helpers the native query operations use (resolveIndexType, assertValidNumericValue, assertValueIndexCompatibility); queryOp is omitted rather than sent as undefined because WASM serde rejects undefined.

Errors throw rather than returning the native {data}|{failure} Result envelope, consistent with the existing WASM encrypt/decrypt; null/undefined plaintext returns null without calling the FFI; bulk path is position-stable with null passthrough and the first invalid term aborts the batch.

The declared return type is EncryptedQuery | null, but for searchableJson with a string value the method returns a bare selector-hash string, which EncryptedQuery does not include (the native client's EncryptedQueryResult does).

CI: the Drizzle integration workflow now triggers on packages/stack/src/wasm-inline.ts and runs a new integration/wasm family suite; the stack integration vitest config un-stubs the protect-ffi and auth wasm-inline modules for all integration suites; e2e/wasm gains a query-types suite and a deno.lock.

Public docblock examples for the raw SQL shapes (casts to eql_v3.query_<domain>, =, @>, -> with selector) and guidance that query terms are 'safe to log-scrub less aggressively than storage payloads'.

failure_scenarios.title: Declared return type omits the bare selector string returned for searchableJson selectors
failure_scenarios.trigger: A TypeScript consumer calls encryptQuery('$.path', { queryType: 'searchableJson' }) (or a bulk term with a string value on an ste_vec column) and handles the result as the declared EncryptedQuery object.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: encryptQuery is typed Promise<EncryptedQuery | null> (wasm-inline.ts:443) and EncryptedQuery is only the two envelope object types (types.ts:72-74), but the docblock (wasm-inline.ts:416-421) and the e2e test (query-types.test.ts:159-165, which needs `as unknown as string`) confirm the selector path returns a plain string. The native client types the same result as EncryptedQueryResult, which includes string (types.ts:333).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Type-guided code (e.g. reading term.v, or JSON-serialising it before binding as jsonb, giving a quoted string) compiles but builds a wrong selector argument; JSON path queries return no or wrong rows silently. Fixing the type later narrows/widens a published signature.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Widen the return types to EncryptedQuery | string | null (mirroring EncryptedQueryResult) before release, or add overloads keyed on queryType/value type.

failure_scenarios.title: JSON containment/selector terms never matched against a real EQL database
failure_scenarios.trigger: An edge consumer uses the documented searchableJson recipes (prefs @> term::jsonb::eql_v3.query_jsonb, prefs -> selector).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The WASM integration adapter's SUPPORTED_OPS (adapter.ts:39-54) covers only scalar ops; the e2e query-types suite only checks term shape (v3, no ciphertext). Nothing executes the JSON SQL shapes from the docblock against Postgres, unlike every scalar query type.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If the WASM-minted ste_vec needle or selector, or the documented cast/operator, does not match what the installed EQL v3 SQL expects, JSON queries silently return no rows (or error) on the edge.

missing_verification: Live row-matching test for searchableJson containment and selector via the WASM entry
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add JSON ops to the WASM adapter (or a dedicated integration test) before advertising JSON search on the edge; otherwise mark it experimental in the changeset.

failure_scenarios.title: Public guidance invites logging query terms that leak equality/order relationships
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer follows the docblock note that query terms are 'safe to log-scrub less aggressively than storage payloads' and logs them.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: wasm-inline.ts:371-375 states terms are safe to log-scrub less aggressively. Terms carry HMAC, bloom and ORE/OPE material derived from plaintext; logged terms correlated across requests or against stored rows reveal equality and ordering of searched values.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Search-term metadata (who searched for what, and order/equality relationships) leaks into log stores outside the encryption boundary. Not plaintext, and no key is exposed.
missing_verification: Security review of the documented logging guidance
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Reword the docblock: treat query terms as sensitive (do not log), consistent with the repo's 'do not log plaintext' rule.

coverage_limitations.description: Lock-context / identity binding: the WASM entry (before and after this change) has no withLockContext, while the native query path forwards lockContext. Whether WASM-minted terms match rows written by a native client under a lock context depends on ZeroKMS/EQL index-key derivation, which could not be checked offline.
coverage_limitations.effect: Mixed native/edge deployments using lock contexts are not assessed; this limitation predates the change, so it is not raised as a scenario.

coverage_limitations.description: Docblock SQL shapes using bare operators (email = term::eql_v3.query_text_eq, @>) were not checked against the EQL v3 SQL bundle; the integration adapter uses eql_v3.eq/contains functions instead.

evidence.claim: encryptQuery returns null for null/undefined plaintext and otherwise calls wasmEncryptQuery with toFfiQueryTerm; typed Promise<EncryptedQuery | null>.
encryptQueryBulk filters null values, sends {queries} to wasmEncryptQueryBulk, and reassembles results at original indices.
toFfiQueryTerm runs assertValidNumericValue, resolveIndexType and assertValueIndexCompatibility and omits queryOp when absent.
The shared resolver imports protect-ffi as type only and runtime values only from ../../types, so importing it into the WASM entry does not pull the native FFI.
EncryptedQuery is a union of two envelope types with no string arm; EncryptedQueryResult (line 333) includes string.
Docblock documents JSON containment via @> and that a selector returns the BARE selector-hash string bound to ->.
e2e asserts typeof selector === 'string' and must cast `as unknown as string`, showing the declared type does not admit a string.
Docblock says query terms are safe to log-scrub less aggressively than storage payloads.
WASM adapter SUPPORTED_OPS covers eq/ne/in/notIn/range/matches/order/null ops only; no JSON containment or selector op.
